newsitem.title: USA: Rorer seeks Lovenox FDA ok for angina.
newsitem.headline: Rorer seeks Lovenox FDA ok for angina.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc said Wednesday that it submitted a supplemental new drug application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for Lovenox (enoxaparin sodium) injection.
The company said it is seeking marketing clearance for Lovenox to be administered with aspirin in the treatment of patients with unstable angina and non-Q-wave myocardial infarction.
Rhone-Poulenc is majority owned by French chemicals group Rhone-Poulenc SA.

Unstable angina is a condition characterized by severe chest pain and is caused by a decrease in blood and oxygen to the heart muscle. It can occur when the patient is at rest or during minimal exertion. This type of angina prompts emergency hospitalization since it signals an increased risk of heart attack and death.

The application filed with the FDA was based in part on an international clinical study, known as the ESSENCE trial (Efficacy and Safety of Subcutaneous Enoxaparin in Non-Q-Wave Coronary Events), which showed Lovenox to be more effective than unfractionated intravenous heparin in reducing the combined endpoint of death, heart attack or recurrent angina (chest pain) in patients diagnosed with unstable angina or non-Q-wave heart attack. A non-Q- wave heart attack is a condition characterized by partial damage to the heart wall due to blockage in the coronary artery.

The multicenter ESSENCE trial was a randomized, double-blind clinical trial conducted at 176 centers in 10 countries in North and South America and Europe. The trial compared the safety and efficacy of enoxaparin to unfractionated heparin in 3,171 patients with unstable angina or non-Q-wave heart attack.
